name: AdvancedEncryption.WE.Praxis.period_iff_and_ratio
title: Canonical names make (a, b) -> name(a + b tau) periodic exactly on a + b tau = 0, and any nonzero period reveals tau
statement: Let K be a field, nu : K -> X injective (a canonical name of a plaintext) and tau in K. For f(x, y) = nu(x + y tau): (1) (a, b) is a period of f, that is f(x + a, y + b) = f(x, y) for all x, y, iff a + b tau = 0; (2) every nonzero (a, b) with a + b tau = 0 has b != 0 and tau = -a / b. This is the algebraic core of the quantum key-recovery attack in note pq-we-praxis-bilinear-substitutes: if an encoding supports Praxis decryption (F_q-linear combinations, the pairing and canonical names of target elements), the map (a, b) -> name(e(a P_0 + b P_1, B)) on two quotient powers P_k = [zeta tau^k]_1 has this form, so Shor's period finding recovers tau and then the key.
